title: Deferred SLA mapping and workload onboarding protocol for Dedicated Pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Customers requesting Dedicated (reserved) GPU capacity often provide incomplete workload signals at intake (e.g., sample QPS but not tail-percentile latency under live traffic, or model quantization constraints). Current intake assumes the team can make immediate SLA commitments; that risks either over-provisioning or needing disruptive mid-contract changes.

Goal:
Create a lightweight, repeatable protocol to 'defer' final SLA banding until we collect a short pre-onboarding signal period and run a deterministic mapping heuristic that ties: workload fingerprint, requested throughput, model family and token distribution -> recommended GPU class, reserved throughput, canary scaling policy, and fallback ladder. Outcome should reduce over-provisioning by >=20% for customers with typical bursty patterns while keeping SLA miss rate <1% during the probe period.

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise Dedicated intake only (non-bug).
- Produces: intake questionnaire, scoring rubric, short validation step (2–7 day probe), automated recommendation (GPU family + reserved throughput + burst policy + canary config), optional engineering runbook items.
- Does NOT change pricing contract language (commercial team to approve).

Key concepts in the protocol:
1) Deferred mapping window: after initial intake call, customer is provisioned a small reserved pool (sized conservatively) for a probe window (default 72 hours, configurable). During the window we collect tail latency (95/99), cold-start measurements, and KV/prefix cache hit rates on sample workloads.
2) Fingerprint vector: a compact set of signals used by the heuristic: peak QPS, mean tokens per request, 95p length, model_arch (e.g., Llama2/Redwood-vX/Claude-style), batching sensitivity, acceptable p95 latency (customer input), and tolerance for quantization.
3) Heuristic scoring: compute three scores (LatencyRisk, CostSavingsOpportunity, ScaleFragility) using weighted rules. Example formula (text):
   - LatencyRisk = w1*(95p_length / GPU_context_capacity) + w2*(batching_sensitive ? 1.0 : 0.3) + w3*(model_attention_type_penalty)
   - CostSavingsOpportunity = w4*(supports_quant ? 1 : 0) + w5*(high_cache_hit_rate ? 1 : 0)
   - ScaleFragility = w6*(burst_ratio) + w7*(observed_cold_start_rate)
   These map to bands: SLA-Critical, SLA-Standard, SLA-Flexible.
4) GPU mapping heuristics (example guidance):
   - SLA-Critical + long sequences -> prefer A100-80GB or H100-80GB w/ higher concurrency lanes.
   - SLA-Standard + batch-friendly + high cache -> prefer A10 or T4 family in deduped quantized format.
   - SLA-Flexible -> recommend smaller GPU classes with autoscaling and burst credits.
5) Canary/Scaling policy template: default canary deploy (10% traffic, 30 minutes) and scaling steps tuned to the probe traffic percentiles. Include automatic fallback to cheaper model variant when p99 latency exceeds target for >3 min.

Deliverables:
- Intake questionnaire (embedded below) that PMs/solutions engineers will use.
- Scoring rubric and mapping matrix (document + JSON config for automation).
- Probe window dashboard template (Grafana link) with required panels.
- Runbook snippet for infra engineers for safe rollback and capacity adjustments.

Sample intake questionnaire (fields):
- Customer name
- Contact / SE owner
- Primary workload (chat/generation/embedding/rerank)
- Estimated steady QPS and expected peak QPS
- Typical tokens per request (mean, 95p)
- 95p acceptable latency (ms)
- Model family and variant (or requirements for closed-source)
- Quantization tolerance (none/int8/q4)
- KV/prefix cache expected reuse (low/medium/high)
- Data residency / encryption constraints
- Canary acceptance criteria (boolean list)

Acceptance criteria:
- A showable matrix that, given a fingerprint vector, returns a deterministic recommended GPU class and reserved throughput (documented examples: 10 fingerprints -> correct mappings covered).
- Probe window dashboard produces 95/99 latency and cache metrics and a generated recommendation within 72 hours of probe data collection.
- PM and frontline SEs can complete intake in 15 minutes using the questionnaire.
- Pilot with two existing enterprise accounts results in <= 10% post-onboarding SLA re-negotiations during the first 90 days.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: customers with adversarial burst patterns still cause SLA misses. Mitigation: clear contract clause + real-time fallbacks + burst credit policy.
- Risk: heuristic inaccuracies for new open-model families. Mitigation: conservative defaults + rapid ML-onboarding ('model spec file' ingestion).

release_notes: Adds deferred SLA mapping protocol and intake questionnaire to reduce premature over-provisioning and improve Dedicated onboarding accuracy.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates recommendation (PM layer) from enforcement (infra config). The automation component will output a human-readable recommendation; infra teams will be asked to approve any non-conservative provisioning changes.
